subject: admission-queue
note: Speculative prefetch arrivals were enqueued into a 50-deep queue drained at the live concurrency limit; under congestion a promoted prefetch lands after its value window. A/B on the real PriorityQueue across BandwidthDetector's tiers: 3g 52 dispatches/18 useful -> 30/30; 2g 17/5 -> 10/8; 4g no-op (never saturates). Skipping hover too served 0/6 hover prefetches, so the source exemption is load-bearing.
return_condition: Re-measure with real hitRate/unused counters from a throttled browser session; the useful/wasted split currently rests on a modelled value window.

subject: admission-queue
note: maxSize/maxConcurrent are count bounds while the scarce resource is bandwidth. BandwidthDetector already derives the count from the network tier, which is load-aware-admission done correctly. Whether payload cost varies enough here to justify byte denomination is unknown - the analytics record hit rate and usage but not response size per prefetch.
return_condition: Instrument per-source response size in PrefetchAnalytics; if the p95/p50 ratio exceeds ~10x, re-test byte-denominated admission against the count bound.

subject: settings
note: WidgetConfig.theme carries a distinct auto value meaning follow-the-viewer -- an inherited default. Both resolution points reduce it to THEME_PRESETS.dark server-side, where the viewer preference is invisible; ThemeCustomizer even documents the gap in a comment (could check prefers-color-scheme on client) rather than closing it. Shipped. Verified A/B on the REAL functions extracted from HEAD vs the working tree, n=2 viewer environments: arm A serves the environment-appropriate palette to 1/2, arm B (emit the light palette as base plus a prefers-color-scheme dark block, resolving where the source is visible) serves 2/2. Instrument self-asserted: arms identical on explicit light/dark, and an explicit pin does not move when the viewer preference changes. The route already emits an inline style block, so arm B needs no new mechanism. Shipped to main as facc957 (not pushed): auto now emits the light palette as base plus a prefers-color-scheme dark block redefining the same six custom properties. typecheck 29 errors before and after with 0 in this file; eslint clean.
structural_fact: The three-state MODEL survived intact; the subscription was destroyed at the resolution point, twice, in two files, by two code paths -- one of which had written the problem down. Shape and semantics were maintained by different hands and only shape reached the renderer. Preserving the model protects nothing on its own; the rule must bind where resolution happens.
instrument_named: none needed -- the A/B is deterministic on emitted CSS
return_condition: if the embed becomes size-budgeted, price the second palette; a consumer rendering into a context with no environment preference should pass an explicit value rather than have the renderer invent one
commit_note: ThemeCustomizer.resolveColors() carries the identical defect and was deliberately left alone - its consumers render one resolved palette with no media-query block, so returning light there would make them light-only. That seam needs its callers changed with it.

subject: measurement-honesty
seam: src/app/features/Collection/hooks/useVisibleCollectionItems.ts:140-159 (completionPercentage) and useCollection.ts:319 (the denominator it was handed)
note: completionPercentage is a ratio over the grid but its denominator was pageSize, passed under the comment "use page size as proxy for grid size", while its numerator (placedCount) counts matched cells across the WHOLE grid. Different populations, then Math.min(x,100) to hide it. Found by the clamp: the store's own computeGridStatistics needs no clamp because there both terms count over gridItems. Shipped. A/B on the project's own instrument over the 120 reachable states (capacities 5-50, page sizes 20 and 50, three page-fill states), each arm scored against the ratio the grid store computes for the same inputs: arm A 66/120 (55%) percentages wrong, 21 isComplete wrong, 9 clamped; arm B 0 wrong on all three. A five-slot grid with one placed item showed 2% against the store's 20%, and CollectionStats renders that figure green at >=100, so the clamp was surfacing a false complete badge. Computation extracted as computePlacementStats and pinned by 6 new tests; the impossible state now warns in dev rather than being clamped. typecheck 29 before and after with 0 in these files; vitest 281 passing (was 275); eslint 0 errors, 3 warnings before and after.
structural_fact: The correct denominator was already on the object the consumer held. The hook subscribes to the grid store and reads placed ids off `state`; that same `state` carries maxGridSize (the real capacity) AND gridStatistics (the already-correct percentage). It reached past both for a page size imported from another module. Nobody designed that - a duplicate implementation of a published quantity usually means the consumer lacked the denominator, and a defensive clamp is where that shows.
instrument_named: none needed - the A/B is deterministic on a pure function, and the sweep is now a committed test
return_condition: If a second implementation of a grid-derived figure appears, consume gridStatistics directly instead of recomputing. Separately: cowGridUpdate (grid-store.ts:259-290) patches matchedCount incrementally while computeGridStatistics - the full recomputation - sits in the same file and is never called to arbitrate it. The arbiter exists and nothing calls it; worth wiring a periodic or dev-mode reconciliation.
commit_note: The prediction that the Math.min clamp was the defect was FALSIFIED en route: it fires in only 9 of 101 flagged states and never in the shipped configuration (pageSize 50 >= max capacity 50). The defect is the denominator; the clamp is its fingerprint. Removing the clamp alone would have changed nothing and looked like a fix. The docs:unmappedAreas ratchet rise (69->70) is pre-existing and reproduces with these changes stashed - not caused here, not fixed here.
